calls.reason: No AI capex downturn is documented. Microsoft says its lower capex guidance is an accounting change with plans unchanged. One AI-related Nasdaq selloff in October 2026 doesn't establish the predicted chain.
Cursor admitted its pricing change hurt trust. But by November 2025 it reported over $1B in annualized revenue and raised $2.3B at a $29.3B valuation, which runs against his predicted revenue fall.
CNBC, citing sources, reports OpenAI's 2025 revenue at $13.1B, and Reuters gives a similar rounded figure. That is above the $12.7B projection he said it would struggle to hit.
Anthropic's filing shows a Q2 2025 operating loss but revenue slightly above serving costs, and OpenAI's cash burn is unverified. The 'functionality doesn't justify costs' part is largely opinion.
The forecast depends on an AI bust and capex fall, and neither is established. Challenger shows tech layoffs up 54% so far this year, but there is no offshoring data or link to an AI bust.
This is a hedged ('I think') forecast with no deadline. OpenAI's reported enterprise growth and a study of broad enterprise use point against it so far, but nothing settles the eventual outcome.
